A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PEAR study. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SFT-to-GRPO experiments on mathematical reasoning and logic games, together with transfer experiments, ablations, and model-update analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds instruction-following evaluations, proxy-policy experiments, additional baseline comparisons, and DAPO results.

M1.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix A add a proxy-policy adaptation: unavailable behavior probabilities can be replaced by another model's probabilities or a uniform per-token average across three proxies. This changes the inputs to importance weighting. Algorithm 1 and the token, block, sequence, and negative-example objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates mathematical reasoning and logic games. v2 adds instruction following using the SYNTHETIC-2 instruction-following split for SFT, Dolci-RL-Zero-IF-7B for RL, and IF-Eval and IF-Bench for evaluation (Appendix D). This introduces substantially different task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds explicit DFT and Proximal-SFT comparisons on mathematics and SynLogic (Figures 5–6), plus CHORD on SynLogic (Appendix E, Table 9). v1 cited these works but did not report these direct comparisons; its generic single-step importance-weighting baseline is retained.

E3.justification: The main training recipe remains unchanged, but added experiments introduce proxy-model configurations, four clipping ranges evaluated with pre-RL Pass@32/64, block size 8, and DAPO replacing GRPO. RQ1 also relabels the KL reference from the initialization to the behavior-policy symbol while still calling it the base policy; an actual reference-model change is unclear.

E4.justification: v2 adds clipping sensitivity, proxy-policy robustness and probability-correlation analysis, reasoning-marker counts, answer-format checks, and an alternative-RL-algorithm test. Appendix C extends the existing token/block/sequence comparison with block size 8. Earlier negative-example, cross-domain-transfer, and parameter-update analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly reports standard deviations across clipping configurations: 3.95 percentage points for Pass@32 and 2.58 for Pass@64. These describe variation across settings, not repeated-seed uncertainty. The existing 64-response averaging remains; neither version supplies training-seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original Tables 2–4 and the detailed offline/online tables retain their values. Added results include SFT versus PEAR scores of 37.34% versus 57.67% on IF-Eval and 16.67% versus 29.59% on IF-Bench, plus new proxy, baseline, sensitivity, and DAPO results. New Figure 5 reports PEAR AMC23 scores of 59/55 for DS-Qwen/Qwen3-4B, whereas retained Table 2 gives 56/59, without explaining the difference.

T1.justification: The core weighting equations, suffix change-of-measure derivation, support assumption, and return-estimator argument are retained. v1 Appendices B–C become v2 Appendices I–J. The proxy adaptation introduces no new formal derivation or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The central claim about preparing SFT checkpoints for downstream RL remains. The abstract and conclusion replace the 14.6% AIME-2025 headline with 30 percentage points, matching the already reported 5% versus 35% result. The introduction revises the logic-game headline to approximately 25 points, but calls Table 4's Enigmata result SynLogic.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking DS-Qwen's larger gains to cross-family mismatch, proxy effectiveness to probability alignment, and intermediate block sizes to a stability–granularity tradeoff. It also argues that reasoning patterns and answer formats are preserved, discusses approximate teacher access, and explicitly leaves learned-reward RLHF to future work. Earlier mismatch and parameter-drift interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies proxy checkpoint identities, uniform per-token probability averaging, clipping-grid values, and the added experiments' model configurations. Table 2 also clarifies response averaging and cross-benchmark aggregation. Existing training hyperparameters and baseline implementation details are retained; no new code-release or hardware information is supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix E newly positions CHORD, associated with the already cited Zhang et al. (2025a), as an RL-stage method complementary to PEAR's SFT-stage intervention. The related-work discussion and underlying cited works otherwise remain substantially unchanged; citation-letter changes and reference deduplication are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. Local edits repair grammar and cross-references, expand explanations, add an appendix contents page, and remove empty appendix headings. Acknowledgements replace the earlier impact and contribution statements. Added scientific sections do not amount to extensive rewriting of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column formatting to a substantially redesigned single-column layout with colored headings and a new title treatment. Figures and tables are resized and relocated, captions expand, and new comparison and appendix displays are added. v2 Table 11 also extends beyond the right page edge.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical case by testing previously unexamined dependence on exact teacher probabilities, extending evaluation beyond math/logic and GRPO, adding direct comparisons with close baselines, and investigating sensitivity. These additions improve practical applicability and support for the central SFT-to-RL claim. Unreconciled AMC23 scores in Figure 5 versus Table 2 and the introduction's Enigmata/SynLogic mislabel remain reporting weaknesses, but do not outweigh these gains.
